newsitem.title: FINLAND: LEFTIST PARTIES RETREAT IN FINNISH ELECTIONS.
newsitem.headline: LEFTIST PARTIES RETREAT IN FINNISH ELECTIONS.

text.p: SDP and the Leftist Allliance, got 267,153 votes less in
Sunday's municipal election than in the 1995 general election,
which brought them into government, according to preliminary
official results by Statistics Finland on Monday.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's social democrats lost
202,879 votes and the Leftist Alliance received 64,274 votes
less than in 1995. The percentage of votes won by the SDP in the
local government election fell to 24.5 from 28.3 in 1995.
The opposition Centre Party, shed 33,874 votes, but its
share of votes rose to 21.7 percent from 19.8 percent in 1995.
The Centre Party, divided on Finnish membership of the EU
and openly sceptical about EMU, did even better in Finland's
first ever European Parliament election on Sunday.
Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's Conservative Party won
more votes in the municipal election than in 1995, but its
performance in the Europoll was weaker.
Analysts summed up the outcome as a victory for ex-PM Esko
Aho's centrists, in particular the party's Euro-sceptics, for
the conservatives, and for opponents to government policy like
Leftist Alliance vote magnet Esko Seppanen, who campaigned
strongly against EMU and the recent link of the markka to ERM.
